title: Indie hacking became the status quo: how it replaced the Lean Startup
summary: Levels argues indie hacking, which got big around 2016, has completed a 7-year cycle and been absorbed into mainstream startup thinking. It effectively updated the Lean Startup: skip customer interviews, prototype fast, launch, kill what fails, and market by building in public.

principles.text: Skip customer interviews; go straight to lean prototyping and launch fast.
principles.quote: no customer interviews, just go straight to lean prototyping, launch fast, throw stuff at the wall and see what sticks

principles.text: Kill projects that don't work and move on to the next one quickly.
principles.quote: nuke it if it doesn't work and go on to the next project while broadcasting your journey publicly as marketing

principles.text: Broadcast your building journey publicly; it serves as your marketing.
principles.quote: broadcasting your journey publicly as marketing

principles.text: Indie hacker principles are now a default mindset for any startup founder to consider.
principles.quote: indie hacker principles are now part of any startup founder's mindset to at least consider

principles.text: New founders are indie and nomadic by default, yet open to raising funding later.
principles.quote: The new Gen Z founders are indie hackers and nomads by default, while also open to raise funding later
